- **T-004 (V-3) — re-derived, deliverable already present** (major): T-004's deliverable already exists in the working tree, uncommitted: tests/doctor.bats now contains a case titled exactly `doctor: a tracked but uninstalled formula is reported`, with a homebrew_section() helper, asserting on both the branch heading and the fixture formula name. T-004's own design is sound — every fact I checked is right: the doctor's missing-formula branch is exactly dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-doctor:58-68, the brew stub `printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\n:\n'` is at tests/doctor.bats:52, the chezmoi source-path stub is at :33, and doctor.bats had 10 @test blocks at 1dec91c. The problem is the same as T-001's: the task is written as pending work that has in fact been done, so its checker cannot tell a worker's contribution from what was already there.

- **DEC (plan of record vs repo state)** (major): The decomposition I was asked to audit has already been partly executed, and no task file records it. .agent-guild/state/log/dispatches.log shows worker-standard on T-001 at 22:35:06, worker-craft on T-002 at 22:35:58, worker-standard on T-004 at 22:37:18, and two checker-deterministic dispatches at 22:45:06 — all before this DEC-audit was dispatched. Meanwhile every task file still reads `status: pending`, `retries: 0`, `artifacts: []`; .agent-guild/state/verdicts/ holds no T-NNN verdict; and .agent-guild/state/notes/ holds T-001.md and T-004.md. T-002's dispatch left no trace at all — none of the four install scripts is modified. Auditing a decomposition whose statuses are stale means the DAG I am checking is not the DAG being run: the ordering findings above (T-002 checked before T-003 exists, V-2 checked before install-failures.bats exists) have already materialized once rather than being hypothetical. The plan and the repo need to be reconciled before any re-dispatch, or the retry ladder will count attempts against workers for work already sitting in the tree.

- **Spec coverage (AC1–AC8)** (info): Walked all eight acceptance criteria against what the tasks actually build, not against clause citations. AC2 (CLI absent still exits 0 and says it skipped) — built by T-002 requirement 1, proven by T-003's four `absent tool skips clean` cases; covered. AC3 (failure distinguishable from skip by wording) — T-002 requirement 3, judged under B-2; covered. AC5 (dotfiles-doctor reports the package) — T-004, with a real mutation proof; covered. AC6 (last-sync.log) — recorded non-goal at constitution.md:292, correctly not reinstated by any task; I re-derived the reason independently and it holds: dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync never runs `chezmoi apply`, so the installers' output cannot reach a log it truncates every run. AC7 (four sites converted, macOS defaults guards untouched) — T-002 under B-1, scope held by T-006 under D-1/D-3; covered. AC1, AC4 and AC8 are built by T-002 and T-003 but never verified at HEAD — see the first finding. The spec's 'Done when' clause about a live end-to-end apply is correctly assigned to the user by D-4 and the constitution's non-goals, and no task reinstates it.

- **T-002 scope (is it one dispatch?)** (info): Judgment asked for: T-002 converts four sites and carries six clauses in one dispatch. Keep it as one task. The four conversions share a single output contract that the constitution deliberately concentrated in one clause — B-2 is 'the only clause describing what the converted scripts print', and its requirement 3 (skip and failure read differently, 'neither borrows the other's phrasing') is judged across the four scripts as a set, not per script. Four parallel workers would produce four wordings and the judgment check would then be arbitrating between siblings rather than checking a contract. B-1 exists precisely to make partial conversion a failure, which is an argument for one owner of all four. The volume is also modest: the four sites are one `brew bundle` line, one loop body, one loop body, and two function bodies. The real cost of the single dispatch is the retry ladder — a FAIL on any of six clauses re-dispatches all four conversions — and that cost is acceptable given the diagnosis is copied verbatim into the task. The check_method thinness noted above is a separate defect and is fixable without splitting.
  evidence: constitution.md:87-98 (B-2 owns output, requirement 3 is cross-site); T-002.md:5 (six clauses)
- **Ordering (T-003 after T-002 vs V-1's baseline table)** (info): Judgment asked for: the T-002-before-T-003 ordering does not corrupt V-1's per-case baseline table. V-1's mutation builds a fresh worktree at 1dec91c and copies only tests/install-failures.bats into it, so T-002's conversion — whether uncommitted or committed — never reaches the scripts under test there, and SRC="${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/.." resolves inside the worktree. The ordering hazard runs the other way, and it is the second finding above. One caveat neither the clause nor T-003 states, which a worker or checker could trip on: `chezmoi execute-template` resolves `{{ include ... }}` against the configured chezmoi source directory (the real repo), not against SRC, so inside the baseline worktree the script body is baseline but the included data files come from the live tree. Harmless for this job — no task may touch dot_config/vscode-extensions.txt, dot_config/raycast-extensions.txt or the encrypted plugin manifests, and D-1's allowlist forbids it — but worth one sentence in T-003 so nobody 'fixes' it with an absolute --source and defeats the mutation.
  evidence: constitution.md:176-181 (worktree + cp); constitution.md:155 (SRC relative); tests/licensed-fonts.bats:22 (the execute-template pattern)
- **Routing** (info): Judgment asked for: the executor tiers and checker families are defensible, including the two mixed tasks. Executors: T-001 and T-003 and T-004 are clear-spec implementation judged on correctness → worker-standard/sonnet; T-002 (output wording, comment register) and T-005 (prose through the humanizer) and T-006 (commit messages) are taste work → worker-craft/opus. T-003 is the hardest task in the job — fifteen cases, a render/execute environment split, and an exact per-case baseline table — and sits at the top of what 'clear-spec' should carry; the spec it is given is unusually complete, so sonnet is a fair first rung and the ladder exists for the rest. Checkers: T-001/V-2, T-004/V-3 are wholly script-checked → checker-deterministic, correct. T-005/D-2 is wholly rubric → checker-judgment, correct. T-002 (B-1 and B-3 deterministic, B-2/B-4/B-5/B-6 judgment) and T-006 (D-1 and most of D-4 deterministic, D-3 and one D-4 bullet judgment) mix, and both route to checker-judgment. That is the honest direction to err: an opus judgment checker can run a written-out grep, whereas a haiku deterministic checker cannot judge whether a comment carries weight or whether a skip line and a failure line read differently. Both check_methods write the deterministic commands out rather than gesturing at them, which is what keeps the judgment checker from 'reading' its way past a grep. T-003 citing B-3 (deterministic) with checker-deterministic is consistent — the defect there is the missing HEAD run, not the family.
  evidence: CLAUDE.md routing table; T-002.md:8-22; T-006.md:8-20; constitution.md:98,119,126,133 (judgment clauses) vs :68,:112,:174,:197,:211 (deterministic)
- **T-003 (case titles)** (minor): T-003's check_method requires that 'every required title appears', but neither T-003 nor V-1 enumerates the fifteen title strings verbatim. Both give a pattern (`<script>: absent tool skips clean`) plus a table that names four script prefixes for the absent-tool row only (install-packages, install-vscode-extensions, install-claude-plugins, configure-raycast — note the last two are shortened from run_onchange_after_install-claude-plugins.sh.tmpl and run_onchange_configure-raycast.sh.tmpl). The mapping is derivable, but the checker is checker-deterministic on haiku, and 'derive fifteen exact strings, then grep for each' is not a deterministic operation. A wrong derivation FAILs a correct file. Cheap fix: list the fifteen titles verbatim in T-003's excerpt.
  evidence: T-003.md:10-11, :32-39, :78-86; constitution.md:145-149
- **T-002 (exemplar)** (minor): T-002 tells the worker to read run_onchange_after_restore-agent-skills.sh.tmpl:87 first, as 'the closest thing to the target shape'. Re-derived, that line is `npx --yes skills add "$src" ... || echo "    some skills from $src failed (a name may have changed upstream)"` — an inline per-call `|| echo` that names the source, not a collected end-of-run summary, and it reports the source rather than the individual item. It is a good model for B-2's naming and a bad model for B-3's collect-and-report-once, which the task also imposes four paragraphs later. The task never says where the exemplar stops being a model, and a worker who copies its shape satisfies the paragraph it was pointed at while failing the one after. One clause of qualification would close it.
  evidence: run_onchange_after_restore-agent-skills.sh.tmpl:87; T-002.md:57-58 vs T-002.md:80-90
